Signed-off-by: knight42 <anonymousknight96@gmail.com>

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind flake
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

I added the following debugging:
```diff
diff --git pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go
index e429dc9a645..e2b62c6af47 100644
--- pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go
+++ pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go
@@ -461,6 +461,7 @@ func (c *csiAttacher) waitForVolumeAttachDetachStatus(attach *storage.VolumeAtta
        if err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("watch error:%v for volume %v", err, volumeHandle)
        }
+       klog.Infof("waitForVolumeAttachDetachStatus: watching")

        ch := watcher.ResultChan()
        defer watcher.Stop()
```

and noticed that:

```
=== RUN   TestAttacherWithCSIDriver/CSIDriver_is_attachable
    csi_attacher_test.go:96: attachment found on try 0, stopping wait...
    csi_attacher_test.go:100: stopped waiting for attachment
    csi_attacher_test.go:106: updating attachment csi-5988a16c07b08340b5bb360f76ea9b78d2a5f743091347e7d758253051dc6cad with attach status {true map[] nil nil}
I0816 12:56:56.233589   80627 csi_attacher.go:464] waitForVolumeAttachDetachStatus: watching <--- watcher was created after updating the status of attachment
panic: test timed out after 10s


=== RUN   TestAttacherWithCSIDriver/CSIDriver_does_not_exist_not_set__->_failure
    csi_attacher_test.go:96: attachment found on try 0, stopping wait...
    csi_attacher_test.go:100: stopped waiting for attachment
    csi_attacher_test.go:106: updating attachment csi-fc1b3cde1442bf6cfe265647fbbc1ae0ade3490a32e8bbc35e864ee0624cb4c1 with attach status {true map[] nil nil}
I0816 12:56:58.301347   80664 csi_attacher.go:464] waitForVolumeAttachDetachStatus: watching <--- watcher was created after updating the status of attachment
panic: test timed out after 10s
```

From the above logs, we could tell the root cause is the watcher in attacher https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8f9f2fb2d64f81f1bd8aeb4056c4d01a21d2e910/pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go#L460-L463 was created after we update the status of attachment in the test, so the watcher could not receive the update event and just stuck there.

FWIW, it is worth noting that `TestAttacherAttach` and `TestAttacherAttachWithInline` may also have the same problem, but we do not wait for the goroutine to exit in the test so the problem is masked.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #93970

I love deflaking tests!

@knight42 Is this a flake that causes the test to fail sometimes, or are you saying that it will not cover the intended functionality depending on the race condition?

> uses -race + the `stress` tool

Thanks Jordan, I was already using those, but I think I was holding it wrong.

`stress go test -race ./foo` will returned cached test results unless you add `-count 1`. But precompiled test binary does not cache results.

I was not using a timeout of 10s.

@misterikkit It is recommended to limit the timeout to 10s, or you would have to wait for at least 2min https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3f579d8971fcce96d6b01b968a46c720f10940b8/pkg/volume/csi/csi_plugin.go#L51 to see the failed test.

Now that I've read the csi attacher code, I think the actual bug is in csi_attacher.go and not csi_attacher_test.go. Specifically, we do a Get followed by a Watch with the goal of "wait for desired state". If the state changes between Get and Watch, then we are not guaranteed to see any events from the watcher.

This is the race @knight42 found in test. I would guess it is **extremely** difficult to hit this in prod, but I would prefer the attacher fixed instead of the test.

It may be best to go with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/64429 to actually fix this attacher, in which case I would be fine merging this CL to fix tests.

> Specifically, we do a Get followed by a Watch with the goal of "wait for desired state". If the state changes between Get and Watch, then we are not guaranteed to see any events from the watcher.
>
> This is the race @knight42 found in test. I would guess it is extremely difficult to hit this in prod, but I would prefer the attacher fixed instead of the test.

+1 to fixing the bug instead of changing the test to mask the issue

One option for a short term fix would be to create the watch and then do a Get. That requires a bit of re-plumbing since currently the Get is called before we enter the func that creates the watch.

This creates a different race where we start a watch, events can start filling the watch channel, then we do a get, then we start looping on the watch channel. This means we might see states out of chronological order, but I have a hunch it will be okay.
do you have a pointer to the problematic line in the attacher you tracked down?

The call stack is

- Attach()
  - waitForVolumeAttachment()
    - waitForVolumeAttachmentInternal()
      - waitForVolumeAttachDetachStatus()

Get is in `waitForVolumeAttachmentInternal`:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1c548c328a32c5b6819195760d1abba115ab4969/pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go#L157

Watch is in `waitForVolumeAttachDetachStatus`:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1c548c328a32c5b6819195760d1abba115ab4969/pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go#L460

Hi @knight42, myself and @misterikkit were going to planning to look into the shared informer issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/64429 which may fix this test flake. I wanted to check if you were already looking at this, or if we should continue.

> One option for a short term fix would be to create the watch and then do a Get. That requires a bit of re-plumbing since currently the Get is called before we enter the func that creates the watch.

@misterikkit I am not sure if this would actually fix the flake. Now we call `csiAttacher.Attach` in a separate goroutine, and update the status of attachment in another. It is not guaranteed that attacher is already watching the attachment before we update it in the test.

> Hi @knight42, myself and @misterikkit were going to planning to look into the shared informer issue #64429 which may fix this test flake. I wanted to check if you were already looking at this, or if we should continue.

It would be great if you could look into the issue, please let me know if there is anything I could do, I am willing to help.

In addition, while you are fixing the problem, perhaps you could check if there is any chance to update the signature of `volume.Attacher` to
```go
	Attach(ctx context.Context, spec *Spec, nodeName types.NodeName) (string, error)
```
so that we could specify a shorter timeout in the test, which is helpful for the problem I pointed out here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94031#discussion_r472767229.

> It is not guaranteed that attacher is already watching the attachment before we update it in the test.

I think the tests as written would pass because the attacher would do a GET after the attach is created, so it would observe the desired state and return successfully.

However, at that point, the tests would no longer be exercising the intended code. I think the tests should also be refactored to more carefully test the right scenarios. It is best to avoid reactors in tests (especially watch reactors) as they can lead to these brittle/flaky scenarios.

@liggitt How would you prioritize de-flaking this test vs refactoring CSI Attacher? The latter will take longer.

> @liggitt How would you prioritize de-flaking this test vs refactoring CSI Attacher?

short-term, deflaking the test is a priority so we can resolve https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93605 and protect the rest of the code base from newly introduced flakes

* if the only way to deflake the test without completely rewriting it means changing the test so it is not actually testing what we care about, then we should treat the relevant controller code as untested and have a high priority issue tracking rewriting the test to actually exercise the controller code
* it also sounds like we've identified at least two bugs in the controller that should be fixed with high priority:
  * starting a get from an individual item's resourceVersion (should start from a list's resourceVersion)
  * not tolerating/retrying a dropped watch
@liggitt looks like this patch could be applied to this PR?

> @liggitt looks like this patch could be applied to this PR?

Doing so requires rewriting the unit tests to correctly respond to list requests with a resourceVersion. That's a larger change that would require careful review to make sure we didn't regress something, so I'd like to separate that from a fix that stabilizes the unit test flake
Thanks for the detailed analysis. @liggitt could you explain why list is preferred over get here? Is it because an empty list still returns a resourceVersion?

> could you explain why list is preferred over get here? Is it because an empty list still returns a resourceVersion?

the resourceVersion of the list is the version of etcd storage and represents a valid version to start a watch from.

the resourceVersion of the individual item represents the last time that item was modified, which could have been a long time ago, and etcd could have been compacted since then, and it might not even be valid to start a watch from

Oh, thank you! I re-read [this](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/#efficient-detection-of-changes) and now I see that we shouldn't have the race condition I described if we correctly handle `resourceVersion` correctly (as per your `List` suggestion)

EDIT: Although I think fakeClient doesn't do resourceVersions at all

/priority important-soon

Note that this is blocking #93605 and full reopen of 1.20, so resolving the test flake in the next few days would be helpful.

From my perspective, I think this fix makes sense because it simulate the real-world situation. What this fix does is waiting for the watcher to start up and then perform the markVolumeAttached() call. In reallife, attaching through VA is not likely to perform faster than the watcher to be established. 

Even if it does happen during this gap, worst case is attach timeout. And the next attach will succeed. So in terms of priority, I think fixing this flaky test sounds good to me. @misterikkit what's your thoughts?

issue_context.title: [sig-storage] TestAttacherWithCSIDriver flakes with timeout error
issue_context.body:
**Which test(s) are flaking**:

TestAttacherWithCSIDriver

**Reason for failure**:

```
--- FAIL: TestAttacherWithCSIDriver (120.07s)
    --- PASS: TestAttacherWithCSIDriver/CSIDriver_not_attachable (0.01s)
    --- PASS: TestAttacherWithCSIDriver/CSIDriver_is_attachable (0.02s)
    --- PASS: TestAttacherWithCSIDriver/CSIDriver.AttachRequired_not_set__->_failure (0.02s)
    --- FAIL: TestAttacherWithCSIDriver/CSIDriver_does_not_exist_not_set__->_failure (120.02s)
```

This is flaking rarely enough that it is not caught by our CI jobs, which currently tolerate up to 2 unit test failures per run (!).

With that toleration removed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93605, this flake has been seen (https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/93605/pull-kubernetes-bazel-test/1293963409628336128).

Reproducible with the following steps:

1. Build a test binary for the affected package:

```
go test -race -c ./pkg/volume/csi
```

2. Stress the affected test using the [stress](https://godoc.org/golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stress) tool (setting the timeout to a generous timeout relative to the normal test runtime of .02 seconds):

```
stress ./csi.test -test.run TestAttacherWithCSIDriver -test.timeout=10s
```

5. Once failures are seen, look at the logs to see the details about the error:

```sh
ls -lat $TMPDIR/go-stress*
cat $TMPDIR/go-stress...<filename>
```

/sig storage
cc @kubernetes/sig-storage-test-failures
